newsitem.title: USA: Bonneville says firm sales near to output capacity.
newsitem.headline: Bonneville says firm sales near to output capacity.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) refrained from offering next-day surplus power because most of its power is being sold under firm commitments, BPA traders said Monday.
"We are running up against capacity on firm sales," said one BPA trader.
She explained that some recent maintenance outages of hydroelectric turbines, at the Grand Coulee dam in Washington and Bonneville dam in Oregon, also tightened power supplies.
And regional loads were described as up slightly from recent levels.

A source at the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation (BuRec), which operates most of the federal hydropower projects in the Northwest, said overall system operations were little changed despite the maintenance work.
"There is always some maintenance going on," she said.
The BuRec source said three units, out of 15, at Bonneville dam were taken off-line Monday, but other units were brought back on at McNary dam.

The BPA trade source said the agency continues to plan for addtional hydropower volumes as spring runoff approaches, including a shutdown as early as Saturday for the 1,158 megawatt (MW) WNP-2 nuclear plant.
